correctness.rationale: The Löwner condition for K=cond(DAD), with Z=λ_min(DAD)D^{-2}, is Z≤A≤KZ. Averaging Z over permutations of the last n−1 coordinates preserves feasibility and yields an exchangeable diagonal optimum without presuming symmetry. The reduced 2x2 block B(x) has one other eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity n−2. det(B−I)=t(n−1)b²(x²−1) determines the min eigenvalue order; the 2x2 eigenratio is minimized by Px+Q/x on 0<x<=1, and λ_max grows on x>=1. Hence the closed minimizer and phase threshold. Independently checked 600 nonsymmetric scaling trials over five parameter configurations and exact n=5 Jacobi eigenvalues; numerical checks support but do not prove global optimality, which follows analytically.

value.rationale: Exact diagonal congruence scaling of a canonical spiked covariance/precision model is a natural preconditioner benchmark. The theorem identifies the sharp mass-imbalance boundary for any possible scaling and a concrete case where a standard heuristic is strictly harmful, so the closed-form fact is a motivated operator-optimization result rather than just a numerical instance.

final_claim: For n>=3, A=I+tuu^T with t,a,b>0 and u=(a,b,...,b), optimizing the condition number of DAD over all positive diagonal D is attained by D=diag(min(1,sqrt(Q/P)),1,...,1), where P=1+ta² and Q=1+t(n-1)b²; scaling strictly improves over D=I precisely when a²>(n−1)b², with exact piecewise condition number and an explicit n=5 case in which Jacobi equilibration worsens conditioning.
